pr_title: spi: spi_mcux_lpspi: Update delay time to fast spi
pr_body:
Spi using default config 500K cal delay time.
It will cause spi slow.
Now update delay time by spi clock.

Signed-off-by: Frank Li <lgl88911@163.com>

May fix #24939

issue_context.title: LSPI of NXP i.MX RT timing delay issue
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
1. Zephyr Can't update DBT/SCKPCS/PCSSCK to nxp_hal according to spi rate， cause spi transfer slow.
2. The delay time calculated by nxp_hal has an overflow problem，will casue no update  DBT/SCKPCS/PCSSCK,cause spi transfer slow.


I submitted 2 pr to solve these problems：
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/hal_nxp/pull/36
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/23918
comments: @MaureenHelm could you please take a look?

@MaureenHelm  Thanks for your reply
1. for delay time:When the spi speed is configured to be relatively high, the delay calculated by 500K will greatly reduce the transmission rate. The following is an example of 5M. Looking at the overall transmission at a time, the actual transmission speed is only slightly higher than 500K, but far below 5M .
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3456246/82732889-cf53cf00-9d42-11ea-9134-1243448297f3.png)
 2. After the master transfer is completed,if the sr flag is not clear, the callback of the transfer
completion will be called again in other interrupts. You can use the following method to reproduce：
       Call spi_wirte about 150K Byte , Measure the time used by spi_write, under normal circumstances it will take some time, this time will become 0 once issue occur. The occurrence of issues is random and cannot be recovered once it occur. The speed of SPI is set between 20M ~ 25M, which is relatively easy to copy.

@MaureenHelm 
I raise https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/25566 to tracking interrupt issue. This issue to keep tracking time delay. Do you think it is ok？

review_comments: I am missing a comment or commit log describing exactly why the delays are calculated like this.
The delays calculated refer to hal_nxp https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/hal_nxp/blob/master/mcux/drivers/imx/fsl_lpspi.c LPSPI_MasterGetDefaultConfig, Please help check it, Thanks

I do understand what the delays are used for. I am asking why you decided to calculate them this way.

Are you calculating them this way based on the timing of a specific device? Is the calculation based on an application note? Are you aiming for a minimum value? If yes, why not simply pass `0` and have the NXP HAL calculate that minimum value?

Currently, I am unable to tell from the code and commit log.

Perhaps it would be better to allow configuring these delays in the device tree? I fear there might be SPI slave devices out there, for which these delays would have to be tweaked.

`LPSPI_MasterGetDefaultConfig` calculates the default values of these delays always assuming a default baud rate of 500 kbps. This change reproduces the same calculation from that hal function, but using the requested baud rate.

However, I'm concerned this optimization could inadvertently break existing applications that have been using the default delays, so I think we should wait to merge it until after the 2.3 release.

As @MaureenHelm mentioned, HAL NXP only calculates the delay at 500K, not the current SPI rate.
RT1052 RM give the  minimum value SCKPCS = one cycle ,PCSSCK
= one cycle, DBT=2 cycle.
I am not  familiar with SPI of rt1052, so I think reference LPSPI_MasterGetDefaultConfig calculate delay value  is a good way.
![timing](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3456246/82731907-8567ea80-9d3c-11ea-8582-3762c1447a8b.png)

@henrikbrixandersen and I discussed this in the release readiness meeting yesterday (his platforms are most affected by this change), and we agreed it's ok to fix this in 2.3 as long as the delays are made configurable through optional device tree properties. If a node doesn't define an optional property, then the driver defaults to this calculation. Can you update your PR to do this in the next couple of days, so it can be included in the release?
